newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria sees number of its heroin addicts growing.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria sees number of its heroin addicts growing.

text.p: Bulgaria, which straddles a traditional drug route from the Middle East to Western Europe, is facing a sharp increase in the number of heroin addicts, a medical official said on Thursday.

"Currently there are more than 30,000 heroin addicts in Bulgaria compared to last year's (roughly) 20,000 and there is a tendency for this figure to grow," Filip Lazarov, head of the National Council on Drug Addiction, told Reuters.
"Every day 30 to 50 young people in the big cities are becoming dependent on heroin," he said, adding that 20 percent of the schoolchildren in big towns had tried some kind of narcotic.
Interior ministry officials said many drug addicts had been forced into crime to supply their daily "fix".
"More than 2,000 drug addicts involved in criminal activities had been registered at the ministry," a ministry spokesman, Razum Daskalov, told a news conference.
He said Bulgaria, with a crisis-ridden economy and population of 8.5 million, was not prepared to fight drug abuse growing after the collapse of communist rule in the Balkan country in 1989.
